scope: Fixture and golden-file contract for every source-comparison / replay test this team authors.

goldenConsumer.must: An EXPLICIT source replay / fixture test MUST FAIL when its golden file is missing, and MUST FAIL when the golden file is empty (zero bytes, or empty/invalid JSON payload).
goldenConsumer.mustNot: It must never return Ok, never skip, and never appear green when the golden is missing or empty.
goldenConsumer.rationale: A green suite that silently skipped the oracle is a false pass, which is worse than a failure.
goldenConsumer.ordinaryTests: An ordinary test that does not depend on the oracle may run without a golden.
goldenConsumer.diagnostics: The failure message must name the expected file path, the env var that supplies the golden directory, and the generation command.

nodeRuntime.must: Oracle scripts keep their existing pins unchanged (process.version v24.22.1, the v8 version, and the TypeScript version).
nodeRuntime.where: Oracles run ONLY inside the existing capped Node 24.22.1 image sha256:a001f865dc47694124ef59a1f71cdf80e6214f64613f4e5b4d891088f71dca82 through validate.py.
nodeRuntime.hostNode: The host Node must NOT run the oracles. Workers must not invoke host node at all - not to execute an oracle, and not even for a parse-only syntax check. Use a static bracket/quote balance scan instead.
nodeRuntime.modes: Oracle scripts keep exactly the --write DIR and --check DIR modes, writing with the wx flag into an empty external directory.

supersedes: The earlier team lead instruction that a golden consumer should SKIP cleanly when the golden file is absent. That instruction was wrong and was corrected to both lanes before READY.
